publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Single reconfigurable DSP coherent receiver is experimentally demonstrated for mixed-format and bit-rates including QPSK, OFDM, IR-UWB for wireline and wireless signal types. Successful transmission over a deployed fiber link is achieved.

articleTitle: Novel architectures for orthogonal wavelength division multiplexed passive optical networks (OWDM-PONs) in a 25-GHz grid
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel orthogonal wavelength-division-multiplexed passive optical network with 25-GHz channel spacing has been proposed and experimentally demonstrated for the first time. Error-free transmission over 15-km SMF-28 was achieved for both 25-Gb/s downlink and 12.5-Gb/s uplink.

articleTitle: Impact of the channel count on the nonlinear tolerance in coherently-detected POLMUX-QPSK modulation
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: GPU-based transmission simulations with different channel counts (1~81) are used to determine the minimum required channel number for correctly simulating fiber nonlinearities that impact 40G/100G CP-QPSK signals in dispersion un-compensated transmission systems.

articleTitle: Suboptimal ODN design algorithm for minimizing cable deployment cost
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel design algorithm of PON ODN is proposed and demonstrated. Based on the forecasted demand, it can automatically generate a suboptimal network in terms of the total cable deployment construction length under realistic restrictions.

articleTitle: Optimization of carrier phase estimation for 112 Gbit/s PM-QPSK systems
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For 112 Gbit/s PM-QPSK systems, the residual phase noise auto-correlation function with a lag of N can serve as a suitable monitor signal for optimizing the averaging in carrier phase estimation algorithms.

articleTitle: Optical interconnects in future HPC systems
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This talk will describe the primary interconnection network challenges as we attempt to build exascale computers over the coming decade. We discuss the role that optics will play in these systems, and key attributes for signaling technology from a system builder's perspective.

articleTitle: Design green and cost-effective translucent optical networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a network design algorithm to effectively reduce the cost and power consumption of translucent networks by using all-optical 2R regenerators. Simulation results show that the number of O/E/O 3R can be effectively reduced.

articleTitle: Designs of bend-insensitive multimode fibers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: New designs of bend-insensitive multimode fibers are proposed. The bending loss can be reduced by a factor of 10 while meeting all other standard requirements. The design concept is validated by actual fiber results.

articleTitle: Regulation environment around the world: Impacts on deployments
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical access systems aim at covering worldwide requirements. Nevertheless, a great disparity in FTTx deployments between countries is observed. Among several factors, regulation choices play a major role for which after analysis some guidelines will be given.

articleTitle: Time-interleaved phase remodulation to enable broadcast transmission in bidirectional WDM-PONs without additional light sources
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Time-interleaved phase remodulation is proposed to realize broadcast transmission for WDM-PONs. Simultaneous transmission of 5-Gb/s bidirectional unicast data and broadcast data is demonstrated at the same carrier wavelength over a 20-km SMF.

articleTitle: Integrated electrical/optical switching for future energy efficient packet networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Future packet transport networks need to cope with rapidly growing Internet traffic. Hybrid architecture approaches combining limited electronic with massive optical switching can help to overcome the severe cost, energy and scalability issues.

articleTitle: 2-cm spatial resolution over 40 km realized by bandwidthdivision phase-noise-compensated OFDR
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a bandwidth-division phase-noise-compensated optical frequency domain reflectometry technique. Using this approach, we realize a spatial resolution of 2 cm over 40 km in a normal laboratory environment.

articleTitle: Long-distance standard single-mode fiber transmission of 40-Gbit/s 16QAM signal with optical delay-detection and digital pre-distortion of chromatic dispersion
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Dispersion pre-distorted 40-Gbit/s 16QAM transmissions over 800-km standard-single mode fiber (~13300 ps/nm) using delay detection is demonstrated with large tolerance to laser phase noise (1-MHz linewidth DFB laser source) and pre-distortion error (±40-km SSMF).

articleTitle: A broadband, spectrally flat, high rep-rate frequency comb: Bandwidth scaling and flatness enhancement of phase modulated CW through cascaded four-wave mixing
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a scheme to scale the bandwidth by several times while enhancing spectral flatness of frequency combs generated by intensity and phase modulation of CW lasers using cascaded four-wave mixing in highly nonlinear fiber.

articleTitle: WDM multi-channel filter based on sampled gratings in silicon-on-insulator
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The design and fabrication of sampled gratings on silicon-on-insulator rib waveguides is presented. A multiple reflection up to 20 channels with a spacing of 0.78 nm is demonstrated, with potential filtering applications in WDM networks.

articleTitle: Multi-layer grooming and routing in packet-optical networks including WSONs
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A multi-layer grooming and routing method, which considers the optical layer constraints, is proposed. This method, based on a new modeling, allows significant resource saving with respect to a layer by layer approach.

articleTitle: Transmission of 96×100Gb/s with 23% super-FEC overhead over 11,680km, using optical spectral engineering
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We transmit 96 PDM-QPSK channels at 100Gb/s over 11,680km, matching the best capacity × distance product reported, but with C-band-only EDFAs. 2.7b/s/Hz spectral density is obtained, despite 23% super-FEC overhead, with optical spectral engineering.

articleTitle: High-power, low-noise slab-coupled optical waveguide (SCOW) amplifiers and lasers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review the development of a Watt-level semiconductor quantum-well gain medium based on the slab-coupled optical waveguide (SCOW) concept. Devices realized in the 1.5-μm-wavelength region include semiconductor optical amplifiers, single-frequency lasers, and monolithic and external-cavity mode-locked lasers.

articleTitle: OSNR monitoring of a 1.28 Tbit/s signal using a reconfigurable wavelength selective switch
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate in-band optical signal to noise monitoring of an 1.28 Tbit/s signal by implementing an interferometer inside a reconfigurable wavelength selective switch based on liquid crystal on silicon technology.

articleTitle: 100 Gb/s photoreceivers for coherent and direct detection
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Photoreceivers for coherent and direct detection of 100 Gb/s data rates, consisting either of 90° optical hybrids integrated with pairs of balanced detectors forming coherent QPSK photoreceiver OEICs, or pin-diodes with travelling-wave amplifiers, are presented.

articleTitle: Real-time ultra-broadband group delay monitoring through quasi-incoherent processing
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Simple method for real-time ultra-broadband group delay measurement of photonic devices is reported, demonstrating accurate group delay ripple monitoring of a 10m-long chirped fiber grating over the full C band at 15frames/s video rate.

articleTitle: Benefits of closer and methods for automatic cooperation between Packet and Transport networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: When Packet and Transport networks operate autonomously, performance degradations and inefficiencies can occur. Closer automatic cooperation between Packet and Transport networks results in improved performance and efficiency. Copyright 2010 Verizon, all rights reserved.

articleTitle: System impairments and performance implications of ASE seeded WDM PON systems
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Systematic analysis of various impairments in ASE seeded WDM PONs is presented and transmission performance limitations are determined in this paper. From a system perspective, characteristics of colorless transmitters are optimized for larger transmission distance.

articleTitle: Mitigation of nonlinearities in optical transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Nonlinear compensation with digital back-propagation can improve Q-factor by more than 1dB, proven by experiments. Simplification of propagation model is the key to suppress circuit size, whereas straight-forward implementation reaches 30-times larger than linear equalizers.

articleTitle: The Telstra network and transport technology evolution
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Telstra has deployed long haul 40 Gbit/s DWDM transmission and is undertaking 100 Gbit/s transmission trials for ultra-long haul links. Technology evolution options beyond today's NGN Ethernet aggregation and core transport network are being considered.

articleTitle: Ultra-stable radar signal from a photonics-assisted transceiver based on single mode-locking laser
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel RF-generating scheme exploits a commercial optical I/Q modulator to allow using a single mode-locking laser for both radar transmitter and receiver, making the solution attractive for immediate and practical implementation in photonics-assisted transceivers.

articleTitle: Developments and applications of microstructured fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Nowadays, fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) indisputably represent one of the most powerful in-fiber tools for the development of effective sensing and communication devices. Within this fiber technology, the last decade has been characterized by the birth of an emerging class of FBGs, which can be defined as microstructured FBGs. They mainly refer to two large categories: one relies on FBG writing in microstructured optical fibers, while the second deals with standard FBGs where structural defects at micro-scale are properly created within the hosting fiber by post processing techniques. This paper reviews the fabrication processes at the basis of this technology as well as its applications, discussing perspectives and challenges that lie ahead.

articleTitle: Impact of intra-channel fiber nonlinearity on reduced-guard-interval CO-OFDM transmission
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Channel estimation for a reduced-guard-interval (RGI) CO-OFDM system shows a unique dependence on the training symbol design in the presence of intra-channel nonlinearities. Because smaller FFT sizes can be used, the RGI CO-OFDM system also demonstrates better nonlinearity tolerance than conventional CO-OFDM with larger FFT sizes.

articleTitle: Photonic technologies for antenna beamforming
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Among the many photonic technologies available for antenna beamforming, those which provide flat RF response over a very wideband RF bandwidth, high signal to noise ratio, multiple-beam capabilities and minimum complexity are to be preferred.

articleTitle: A novel method for precise symbol synchronization in double-side band optical fast OFDM
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel method to achieve precise symbol synchronization using one training symbol in DSB optical fast OFDM (FOFDM). World-first FOFDM transmission experiment using field-installed fiber verifies its robustness to the noise and CD.

articleTitle: Multi-core fibers for large capacity SDM
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Developments of multi-core fibers, both solid type and holey type, are introduced. The Space Division Multiplexing will be realized by the multi-core fibers.

articleTitle: Integrated Fourier domain mode-locked lasers: Analysis of a novel coherent WDM comb laser
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Fourier-domain mode-locking of integrated laser diodes is studied theoretically for the application of WDM mode comb generation. Flat (<;7 dB) combs with 40 modes spaced at 25 GHz and RIN values of below 0.3% can be generated with practically feasible designs. Such lasers enable future Terabit/s interconnects.

articleTitle: Recent progress in optical fiber refractive index profiling
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Recent optical fiber refractive index profile measurement advances include quantitative phase measurement, multi-wavelength spectroscopy, and computerized tomography. These new techniques, and their application to fiber-based components including tapers, splices, gratings, and couplers, are reviewed and discussed.

articleTitle: Efficient optical packet transport in access, metro, and core networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present and evaluate opportunities and challenges for packet optical transport of residential and business data services from access to core networks. Presented solutions are evaluated based on sample case studies.

articleTitle: Static fatigue characterization with uniform and ultra-small bending
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Static fatigue characteristics with uniform and ultra-small bending are investigated using a proposed slotted bending fixture. The humidity dependence of the time to failure characteristics in HAF is confirmed experimentally for the first time.

articleTitle: Passive mode-locker incorporating physically exfoliated graphene for fiber ring lasers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A passively mode-locked fiber laser is realized using an intracavity intensitymodulating effect in multilayered graphene efficiently prepared by taping method. 10.6-MHz pulse trains with 40-dB extinction rate are guaranteed by the physically exfoliated graphene.

articleTitle: High speed high temperature stable 980 nm VCSELs operating error-free at 25 Gbit/s up to 85 °C for short reach optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present high speed highly temperature stable 980 nm VCSELs for short reach optical interconnects operating error-free at 25 Gbit/s from room temperature up to 85°C without adjustment of the driving conditions.

articleTitle: A novel 1×N demodulator for both DPSK and DQPSK formats
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 1×N demodulator for both DPSK and DQPSK formats is proposed in this paper. The PDFS of such demodulator is less than 300MHz, through introducing LC phase retarder, fast tuning time of 50ms is realized.

articleTitle: Pulsed Fiber-MOPA source operating at 1550 nm with pulse distortion pre-compensation
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper we present a diode-seeded pulsed Fiber-MOPA source operating in the telecommunication band with pulse distortion pre-compensation using arbitrary shaped input pulses. 100 ns long flat-top pulses were obtained.

articleTitle: Fully CMOS compatible subwavelength plasmonic slot waveguides for Si electronic-photonic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Subwavelength horizontal Al/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Al plasmonic slot waveguides with SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> width at each side of ∼15 nm and Si width of ∼136, ∼87, and ∼43 nm are fabricated on SOI substrates using fully CMOS compatible processes. The propagation losses at 1550 nm TE are ∼1.01, ∼1.31, and ∼1.56 dB/µm, respectively, as measured by the standard cutback method. A simple taper coupler with length of ∼0.3–1 µm provides a high coupling efficiency of ∼66%–79% between the plasmonic slot waveguide and the standard Si dielectric waveguide. The plasmonic slot waveguide can achieve a direct 90o bend with a very low bending loss of ∼0.2–0.4 dB. The propagation, coupling, and bending losses depend weakly on wavelength in the c-band. The results demonstrate the potential for seamless integration of functional plasmonic devices in existing Si electronic-photonic integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Demonstration of the self organized dynamic link power management by “MiDORi” energy optimal network topology design engine
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper reports the demonstration results of the dynamic link power management by energy optimal network topology design with prototype Gigabit layer-2 switches. The result shows dynamic link power management is feasible.

articleTitle: Using dispersion in a fiber-optic loop to perform time domain analogue RF signal auto-correlation
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present an RF-photonic time-domain auto-correlator using a dispersion-induced stepped-time-delay of the modulation sidebands produced by a fiber optic recirculation loop circuit. This allows spectrum analysis of a single RF-pulse.

articleTitle: Requirements of low power photonic networks for Distributed Shared Memory computers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Using the PARSEC benchmark suite running on a 32-core Distributed Shared Memory computer system, photonic component and interconnection network characteristics required for reduced overall power consumption are determined.

articleTitle: Optical switch architectures for emerging Colorless/Directionless/Contentionless ROADM networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Next generation reconfigurable architectures are starting to be deployed by carriers worldwide. This paper focuses on emerging Colorless, Directionless and Contentionless (C/D/C) ROADM architectures using optical matrix switches.

PACS Terms: (060.1810) Buffers, couplers, routers, switches, and multiplexers

articleTitle: 32-channel, injection-locked WDM-PON SFP transceivers for symmetric 1.25 Gbps operation
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 32-channel, WDM-PON SFP transceiver is demonstrated at 1.25 Gbps with C-band transmit and L-band receive functionality. The transceiver is based on a wide-band, injection-locked Fabry-Perot laser. Both C-band and L-band SFP transceivers are available.

articleTitle: Signal chirp design for suppression of nonlinear polarization scattering in DP-QPSK transmission
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We analyze chirp techniques for suppression of nonlinear effects in DP-QPSK transmission. Simulations reveal that a significant reduction in nonlinear polarization scattering can be achieved by properly chirping the two polarization tributaries.

articleTitle: Benefits of integrated packet/circuit/wavelength switches in next-generation optical core networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the use of integrated packet/circuit/wavelength switches in next-generation optical core networks and compare different node architectures for a 46 node, 25,840 route-km US network.

articleTitle: Microwave photonic filters with a directly generated Gaussian-shaped optical frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Using electro-optic modulators, we generate a 41-line 10-GHz spaced Gaussian-shaped optical comb. We use this comb to demonstrate apodized microwave photonic filters with greater than 43-dB sidelobe suppression, without the need for a pulse shaper.

articleTitle: Strong fiber Bragg gratings in Bi-Al co-doped H2-loaded optical fibers using CW-Ar+ laser
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Bragg gratings with reflectivity >;93% were fabricated in Bi-Al co-doped H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-loaded optical fibers. Average index changes as high as +2.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> were obtained. Positive core stress changes indicate a compaction contribution to the total index change.

articleTitle: Optimized pulse shaping for intra-channel nonlinearities mitigation in a 10 Gbaud dual-polarization 16-QAM system
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An optimized pulse shape is shown to reduce intra-channel nonlinear effects in a 10 Gbaud dual-polarization 16-QAM EDFA-amplified system without optical dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: PON test systems - From theory to field deployments
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents the first feedback from field experiments of remote fiber testing systems using U band, new High Resolution OTDR and Out-of-band reflective markers installed on the ONT side.

articleTitle: Wavelength-aware translucent network design
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A Wavelength-Aware approach for Translucent design and dynamic routing is presented. Compared to the Wavelength-UnAware worst-case design scenario, up to 100% reduction on OEO interfaces has been found.

articleTitle: ROADM switching technologies
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: ■Wavelength Selectable Switch Technologies -MEMS, LCoS, LC, DLP -Each has design strengths and weaknesses ∂MEMS: strong isolation, small size, low IL, challenged atten accuracy ∂LCoS: strong atten accuracy, flex spectrum, challenged isolation ∂LC: strong atten accuracy, challenged size ∂DLP: small size, flex spectrum, limited port count ■Colorless, Directionless, Contentionless Networks -More efficient use of infrastructure -Requires more complex wavelength switching components ∂Higher port count ∂Multiple input, multiple output

articleTitle: Optical ASK-DPSK and QAM signal generation using FWM in high nonlinearity fiber (HNLF)
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: As a modulation-format transparent nonlinear process, FWM is capable of generating complex optical signal constellations. In experiments and simulations, optical ASK-DPSK and 8-QAM signals are generated with one-step or two cascaded FWM processes, respectively.

articleTitle: Carbon-nanotube and graphene photonics
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Presents a collection of slides covering the following topics: carbon-nanotube; graphene photonics; nonlinear photonics; optical limiter; Raman laser; diamond; photodetectors; band structure; transport properties; nano-FET; dispersion relation; optical absorption; solar cell; nanowires; biosensor; saturable absorption; passive mode locking; Kerr effect; fibre laser; and solid-state laser.

articleTitle: Taking the cost out of short-reach optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Short-reach optical interconnects have enjoyed significant cost reductions over the years competing with copper-based solutions at ever shorter lengths. This talk looks at future developments that may maintain this downward cost trend.

articleTitle: Optical fiber as a conical microresonator
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: High Q-factor localized conical modes are discovered theoretically and demonstrated experimentally in an optical fiber. The theory of these modes provides a means for exceptionally accurate local characterization of the optical fiber nonuniformity.

articleTitle: Phase noise and timing jitter eliminator for mode-locked lasers based on external graphene layers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a noise eliminator with a reduction of 34% for phase noise and timing jitter based on external graphene layers for mode-locked lasers by absorbing the low-power background noise from the laser spontaneous emission.

articleTitle: Cost-effective on-board optical interconnection using waveguide sheet with flexible printed circuit optical engine
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have developed a cost-effective on-board optical interconnection sheet using a polymer waveguide with flexible printed circuit optical engines. Error-free operation up to 14 Gb/s was demonstrated using a 12-ch optical interconnection sheet.

articleTitle: Demonstrating novel functionality of air-holes to realize large-mode-area optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A new functionality of air-holes, worked as prevention for micro-deformation induced loss without affecting other properties, is demonstrated. A fiber with Aeff of 150μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was fabricated by utilizing the new functionality.

articleTitle: Self-coherent receiver for PolMUX coherent signals
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A compact polarization-diversity self-coherent receiver with reduced complexity is proposed. Requirements on input polarization tracking is relaxed by a variant CMA equalizer. Experiments are performed for 50 and 100 Gb/s PolMUX-NRZ-QPSK signals.

articleTitle: Real-time optical OFDM transceivers for PON applications
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Recent real-time optical OFDM (OOFDM) research progress is reviewed extensively in terms of adaptive transceiver design, intensity modulators, synchronisation techniques and network architectures. Results indicate that OOFDM is feasible for mass deployment in PONs.

articleTitle: Impact of transparent network constraints on capacity gain of elastic channel spacing
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We compare fixed-grid network architectures with variable-spacing OFDM based solutions. We show that capacity gains can reach up to 50% but are strongly affected by physical and topological constraints of transparent networks and traffic statistics.

articleTitle: Bit-error rate performance of Nyquist wavelength-division multiplexed quadrature phase-shift keying optical signals
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We measure bit-error rates of polarization-multiplexed Nyquist-WDM QPSK signals, which have rectangular spectral shapes and channel spacing equal to the symbol rate. The spectral efficiency of 4 bit/s/Hz is achieved with negligible power penalty.

articleTitle: Self-starting optical pulsator based 10-Gbit/s RZ-BPSK down-stream and re-modulated RZ-OOK up-stream link
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A synthesizer-free 10-Gbit/s down-stream PRZ-BPSK and re-modulated up-stream RZ-OOK bi-directional transmission with receiving sensitivity of <−17dBm at BER=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup> is demonstrated using a self-pulsating optical carrier with ultralow-jitter of 0.6 ps and high-extinction of 8.5 dB.

articleTitle: Transport network evolution: From TDM to packet
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Transport networks and technologies are undergoing transformation. The genesis of that transformation is packet switching embedded on transport equipment together with DWDM, OTN, and SONET/PDH switching. This paper summarizes the drivers and involved technologies.

articleTitle: “Real world” FTTH optical-to-radio interface performance for bi-directional multi-format OFDM wireless signal transmission
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The optical-to-radio and radio-to-optical interfaces in fiber-to-the-home access networks were evaluated for LTE, WiMAX and UWB simultaneous distribution. Successful bidirectional transmission was achieved after 20.2 km standard single mode fiber and 3 m radio propagation.

articleTitle: Implementation of PCE-based management and control plane for heterogeneous optical networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of an effective PCE-based management and control platform for heterogeneous optical networks. Experimental results show that it works well on network with commercial SDH and OTN equipments.

articleTitle: Transmission experiment using a coupled-cavity VCSEL for radio frequency conversion
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We perform a transmission experiment using a coupled-cavity VCSEL and demonstrate its unique ability for radio frequency conversion. For a short-reach link, the system performance is governed by the dc biasing and local oscillator power applied to the coupled-cavity VCSEL.

articleTitle: Yb-doped Large Pitch Fiber with 105 µm mode field diameter
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present an active Yb-doped Large Pitch Fiber design with 105 μm mode field diameter. The fiber was tested in a fiber CPA system delivering sub 500 fs, 2 mJ pulses with 3.8 GW peak power. The limiting influence of anticrossings on beam quality and average output power is discussed.

articleTitle: Transmission limitations due to fiber nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review recent advances in understanding Kerr nonlinear limitations in high-capacity long-haul coherent systems, with emphasis on PDM-QPSK transmissions. Both homogeneous and hybrid dispersion-managed WDM systems are addressed, as well as homogeneous non-dispersion-managed systems.

articleTitle: OOO switching - The role and technological advances
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical routing technologies will surely be the key to creating future bandwidth abundant and green networks. Considering future services and the need to create virtual fiber networks, the introduction of wavebands is a next important step.

articleTitle: Efficient regenerator placement and wavelength assignment in optical networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a novel auxiliary graph approach for optical networks regenerator placement and wavelength assignment (RPWA) problem. Simulation results show that our proposed approach outperforms other two approaches significantly.

articleTitle: Compact PLC-based transponder aggregator for colorless and directionless ROADM
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We describe a compact transponder aggregator comprising a splitter-switch and a tunable filter array based on PLC technology. We realize a colorless, directionless and contentionless multi-degree ROADM node cost-effectively with a small footprint.

PACS Terms: (060.1810) Buffers, couplers, routers, switches, and multiplexers

articleTitle: Scalable control plane architecture for optical flow switched networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper an OFS architecture that exploits the strength of optics to serve large transactions is described. The shift towards OFS requires some architectural elements of the network- from the physical layer to the higher network layers, as well as network management and control, be substantially redesigned at the fundamental level for the network architecture to be scalable and implementable.

articleTitle: High-precision in-situ wavelength stabilization and monitoring of tunable lasers using AWG and PD arrays
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents a rapid laser wavelength stabilization and monitoring technique based on a feedback loop using AWG with PD arrays at 0.5 MHz. The experiment demonstrates control accuracy of ±0.015 nm on microsecond timescale.

articleTitle: The impact of the combined 8-QAM and QPSK subcarrier modulation for coherent optical OFDM
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigated the optimized signal condition of the combined 8-QAM and QPSK subcarrier modulation for optical OFDM. The performance improvement was confirmed by WDM transmission experiments with the optimized power difference and subcarrier number.

articleTitle: Symmetrical 2-D Hermite-Gaussian square launch for high bit rate transmission in multimode fiber links
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 2-D Hermite-Gaussian square launch is demonstrated to show improved systems capacity over multimode fiber links. It shows a bandwidth improvement over both center and offset launches and exhibits ±5 μm misalignment tolerance.

articleTitle: Comparison of RZ and NRZ formats in 112-Gb/s PDM-QPSK long haul coherent transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show that 112-Gb/s PDM-QPSK coherent transmission systems with RZ pulse shape have better tolerance to ROADM filtering than NRZ, and time-interleaved RZ-PDM-QPSK outperform NRZ-PDM-QPSK in nonlinear transmission even with tight filtering.

articleTitle: High efficiency optical switches with Heater-on-Slab (HoS) structures
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose optical switches in which the heater is fabricated directly on the slab region of the rib waveguide. Two types of Heater-on-Slab (HoS) switches were investigated. In the first type, the silicon slab regions are doped highly to form the heaters. For this type of switches, the switching power is ~85 mW and the switching time is ~27 μs. In the second type, a strip of metal in direct contact with the silicon slab forms the heater. For this type of switches, the switching power is ~25 mW and the switching time is ~17 μs. An extinction ratio of ~28.4 dB was also achieved.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of 16-QAM transmission with a single dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 10-Gbit/s 16-QAM transmission over 160 km with a single dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator was experimentally demonstrated. We achieved BER <; 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> in a BtB condition and <; 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> after the transmission. Electronic pre-equalization was employed to suppress signal distortion.

articleTitle: Photonic waveguide bonds - A novel concept for chip-to-chip interconnects
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Photonic waveguide bonds (PWB) enable three-dimensional chip-to-chip interconnects. We demonstrate for the first time a PWB link between integrated silicon-on-insulator waveguides. The viability of the concept is demonstrated by data transmission experiments.

articleTitle: Bismuth-doped optical fiber amplifier for 1430 nm band pumped by 1310 nm laser diode
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 24dB gain Bismuth-doped fibre amplifier pumped by a 65mW commercial laser diode at 1310nm is reported for the first time. A 3dB bandwidth of 36nm and a noise figure of 6dB are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Compensation of nonlinear effects using digital coherent receivers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Nonlinearity compensation in digital coherent receivers is feasible from a fundamental point of view. This paper shows that it is possible to reduce the computational load required for nonlinearity compensation to practical level.

articleTitle: A novel MAMSK-OFDM technology for next generation optical access networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a novel MAMSK-OFDM-PON. 5-Gb/s MAMSK-OFDM signal and 2.5-Gb/s upstream OOK signal is transmitted over 20km fiber successfully. The results show the prospect of this technology in future optical access networks.

articleTitle: Cyclic prefix free 10-Gb/s OFDM for a DML-based long-reach optical access using joint time and frequency domain equalization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Without using a cyclic prefix, a DML-based 10-Gb/s OFDM at 2.5-GHz bandwidth transmission over 65-km SMF is demonstrated to be possible while maintaining the efficient throughput and short-latency time required for future long-reach access systems.

articleTitle: The merits of reconfigurability in WDM-TDM optical in-building networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Blocking performance of an optical WDM-TDM in-building network is significantly improved by dynamic wavelength routing. We analyse optimum clustering of users which reduces system complexity while largely preserving network performance improvement.

articleTitle: Recent progress on real-time DSP for direct detection optical OFDM transceivers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We describe recent developments in real-time digital signal processing for direct detection optical OFDM transceivers, including the optimization of high throughput FFT algorithms and receiver synchronization.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity and phase noise in high-current photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Great progress has been made in the past decade in developing high-current photodetectors, but the modeling of these devices has not kept pace. The status of the devices and the models is reviewed.

articleTitle: Performance investigation of polarization-multiplexed 16-QAM using all-optical OFDM transmission and digital coherent detection
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We generated a 500-Gb/s AO-OFDM signal with DP-16QAM modulating each subcarrier and detected the signal using coherent detection. We investigated the effects of DSP oversampling and receiver bandwidth using experimental results and numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Novel hierarchical optical cross-connect architecture utilizing dedicated add/drop switches that effectively offer colorless and directionless capability
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Hierarchical optical cross-connect architectures based on dedicated add/drop switches for terminating traffic is proposed. The architecture can significantly reduce switch scale for implementing colorless/directionless/contentionless capabilities.

articleTitle: Towards real-time CO-OFDM transceivers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Real-time CO-OFDM transmitters and receivers for 10.5Gb/s bit-rate implemented in FPGAs are reported applying 10GSa/s converters and entire algorithms for both terminals. The Q-factors are 22.7dB for the transmitter and 17.8dB for the receiver.

articleTitle: 120-Gb/s PDM 64-QAM transmission over 1,280 km using multi-staged nonlinear compensation in digital coherent receiver
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We succeed in the long-haul (1,280km) transmission of a 120-Gb/s PDM 64-QAM signal. The transmission distance was extended from 800 km to 1,280 km by a multi-stage nonlinear compensation technique that mitigates the intra-channel nonlinearities.

articleTitle: Behavior-based authorization policy for multi-domain PCE-based MPLS and WSON
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel path computation authorization policy based on PCEP peer behavior analysis and attack pattern detection is presented. Applicability is demonstrated in multi-domain PCE-based WSON. Experimental validation in MPLS network testbed is provided.

articleTitle: Mode-locked laser array monolithically integrated with SOA and EA-modulator
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The monolithic integration of four 10 GHz multi-colored mode-locked lasers with a 4×1 MMI, a SOA and an electroabsorption modulator has been demonstrated. The lasers produce 2.49 ps Sech<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-pulses with TBP of 0.389.

articleTitle: Compact 4×4 optical cross-connect with add/drop ports using PLC technology
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Compact and practical 4-degree optical cross-connect equipment with add/drop ports is realized for use in connecting ROADM ring networks. Eight 40-channel AWGs and forty 4×4 matrix switches are integrated in a 2-U high chassis.

articleTitle: Impairment-aware PCE in multi bit-rate 10–100 Gb/s WSON with experimental demonstration
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Two impairment-aware PCE architectures suitable for multi bit-rate WSONs are presented. Experimental demonstration is provided on a real testbed including detrimental XPM effects among 10Gb/s OOK and 100Gb/s DP-QPSK.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-flexible ROADMs as network elements
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The continuing need to reduce transmission costs drives the requirement for higher spectral efficiency in optical communication systems. We review here the use of Bandwidth-flexible ROADMs as one of the enablers of higher capacity systems.

articleTitle: Optical interconnects in future servers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical interconnects are common in today's petascale supercomputers, and will become pervasive at the exascale during this decade. Technologies that can meet the challenging technological and economic requirements for the exascale will be reviewed.

articleTitle: Time-resolved error vector magnitude for transmitter mask testing in coherent optical transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel transition-sensitive measurement approach for coherent optical systems. The time-resolved error vector magnitude (EVM), combined with mask testing, is a powerful tool for pass/fail testing of transmitters in coherent systems.

articleTitle: Recent advances in MMF technology for data networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Multi-Mode Fibers (MMFs) have been developed since the early age of optical communications till the more recent explosion of the Ethernet traffic. This paper will review state of the art MMF technology for data communications.

articleTitle: A new scheme of aspherical microlense for efficient coupling high-power lasers to fibers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a new scheme of aspherical microlens (ASM) employing a single-step grinding technique with fully automated process for efficient coupling between the high-power 980-nm laser diodes and single mode fibers. The grinded fiber endface exhibited a double-variable curvature in the major axis, and was clearly observed for both major and minor axes after slight fusion polish. The perfect aspherical shape of the ASM resulted in less grinding offset of 0.2 µm and better curvature radii control that led to high average coupling efficiency of 83 %. The result clearly demonstrated that the performance of the ASM exhibited high average coupling efficiency better than any other grinding techniques to form asymmetric microlenses.

articleTitle: Low power and broadband 2 × 2 silicon thermo-optic switch
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a 2×2 silicon thermo-optic switch which requires a switching power of only ~12.5 mW and has a response time of 5.4 μs. The measured extinction ratio of the switch is >;~20 dB across the C and L communications bands.

articleTitle: Migration based protection for virtual infrastructure survivability for link failure
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a new migratory protection scheme that maps a virtual infrastructure to a substrate network using minimal resources to recover from a single substrate link failure. The efficiency of our solution is shown using simulation.

articleTitle: A modulation scheme for 100Gb/s Minimum-Shift Keying format based on imbalanced bias in IQ components
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose an optical MSK modulation scheme to achieve the 100Gb/s MSK signal with constant envelope and continuous temporal phase shift. The investigation on the transmission performance clearly demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Evolution of commercial EDFAs
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Erbium Doped Fiber Amplifiers (EDFAs) play crucial role in modern optical telecommunication networks. As the networks evolve, commercial EDFAs faces technical challenges that have to be solved within constrains of ever changing industry.

articleTitle: An ultra-compact polarization rotator based on surface plasmon polariton effect
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 3µm long ultra small surface plasmon polariton effect based TM to TE polarization rotator was designed. Effective polarization rotation was achieved in fabricated devices. 10dB PER and 11dB insertion loss were achieved in experiments.

articleTitle: Comparison of OFDMA and SC-FDMA channel access techniques in a passive optical network environment
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For the first time, OFDMA and SC-FDMA (single-carrier frequency division multiple access) are compared experimentally as candidate uplink access techniques for next-generation PONs. Important issues like peak-to-average power ratio, optical beat interference, and symbol delay are studied and experimentally measured.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of XPM compensation for CO-OFDM systems with periodic dispersion maps
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate compensation of XPM for CO-OFDM systems operating in a periodic dispersion map using a low-bandwidth compensator. The nonlinear threshold was increased by 4 dB in a 22.5 Gb/s 400km transmission system.

articleTitle: MLSE-based nonlinearity mitigation for WDM 112 Gbit/s PDM-QPSK transmissions with digital coherent receiver
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the performance of linear equalization combined with MLSE in long-haul transmission. In the nonlinear regime with high launch powers Q-factor improvement up to 1.4 dB is demonstrated with a quaternary state model.

articleTitle: 60-channel bidirectional WDM-PON using a single 32*32 AWGR for 120 wavelengths distribution
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a 60-channel wavelength division multiplexed passive optical network (WDM-PON) with 10-Gb/s bidirectional transmission. A single 32*32 AWGR is used at the remote node to achieve a total system capacity of 1.2 Tbit/s.

articleTitle: 21-GHz single-band OFDM transmitter with QPSK modulated subcarriers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a single-band OFDM transmitter that allows the generation of signals with a bandwidth of up to 21 GHz. Transmission experiments over up to 641 km without optical dispersion compensation demonstrate the performance with coherent reception.

articleTitle: WDM transmission of 152-Gb/s polarization multiplexed RZ-16QAM signals with 25-GHz channel spacing over 15×80-km of SSMF
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate transmission of 20×152-Gb/s PolMux-RZ-16QAM at a channel spacing of 25 GHz (5.68 b/s/Hz) over 15×80-km spans of SSFM. Coherent detection was used to recover the transmitted data and we achieved BER below 3.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>.

articleTitle: Self-protected scheme for wavelength reusable WDM passive optical networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a wavelength reusable WDM-PON scheme using protective interconnection fibers to achieve whole optical distribution network protection. 10Gb/s bidirectional transmission is experimentally demonstrated and protection performance is analyzed.

articleTitle: An optimal tone reservation method for IM/DD optical OFDM transmission in multimode fiber
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose an optimal, yet efficient tone reservation method which enables distortion-free IM/DD optical OFDM transmission with no additional bias. Compared to previous approaches, both spectral and power efficiencies can be improved.

articleTitle: Large-scale photonic integrated circuit for multi-format regeneration and wavelength conversion
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a large-scale silica-on-silicon photonic integrated circuit with 4 hybridly integrated SOAs for multi-format regeneration and wavelength conversion. Power penalty improvement up to 1.5 dB is reported for degraded OOK and PSK signals.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation and improvement methods for low-driving voltage transmitters in long reach PONs
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The performance of two common low-driving voltage (low-ER) sources is experimentally evaluated for long reach PON applications, considering also partial optical dispersion compensation and electronic equalization methods for performance improvement.

articleTitle: Tunable nonlinear frequency conversion of bismuth-tellurite glass holey fiber
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report on tunable parametric generation (PG) and third-harmonic generation (THG) in a 2.9-μm core bismuth-tellurite holey glass fiber. The maximum conversion efficiency was measured to be 0.1% and 0.06% for PG and THG respectively.

articleTitle: Oxide-relief vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers with extremely high data-rate/power-dissipation ratios
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: By using oxide-relief technique, a high modulation-efficiency (9.8GHz/mA<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>) and a high modulation-speed (34 Gbps) with a record-high data-rate/power-dissipation ratios (2.9 (9.2) Gbps/mW at 34 (12.5) Gbps) of 850nm VCSELs have been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Scheduling of GMPLS path services using switched and fixed paths
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper describes distributed scheduling based on schedule-aware network elements using switched path LSPs whose physical path may vary during service. This technology provides more reliable, more efficient service to better meet user needs.

articleTitle: Fiber nonlinearity management - From carrier perspective
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Technologies for fiber nonlinearity management for spectrally-efficient high-speed optical transmission systems have been discussed from a carrier perspective. While optimal electrical dispersion management remains an effective method, new ultra-low-nonlinearity fiber could provide additional benefits.

articleTitle: Bandwidth scalable, coherent transmitter based on parallel synthesis of multiple spectral slices
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents a bandwidth-scalable, coherent optical transmitter based on the parallel synthesis of multiple spectral slices. As a proof-of-principle, two spectral slice, 6-ns DPSK and QPSK waveforms at 12 Gsymbols/s are generated and measured.

articleTitle: Over 40 GHz traveling-wave electroabsorption modulator based on hybrid silicon platform
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A hybrid silicon traveling-wave electroabsorption modulator has been demonstrated. 43 GHz bandwidth and over 10 dB static extinction ratio are achieved for a 100 µm long device.

articleTitle: Radio over fiber technology for next-generation e-health in converged optical and wireless access network
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Development of system technology for effective networking infrastructure for next generation e-health applications is addressed. An integrated optical wireless access architecture based on radio-over-fiber technology is proposed in order to provide super broadband, ultra low-latency connectivity among various telemedicine modalities to facilitate real-time and near real-time communication for remote health care services.

articleTitle: Wide bandwidth, low loss 1 by 4 wavelength division multiplexer on silicon for optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an add/drop filter based on coupled vertical gratings on silicon. The concept is extended to implement a 1 by 4 wavelength division multiplexer with 3nm bandwidth, 1dB insertion loss and 16dB crosstalk suppression.

articleTitle: 4096-ary OCDM at 2.5 Gbit/s using multidimensional PSK codes with a single multi-port encoder/decoder
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A record 4096 (= 16 × 16 × 16)-ary OCDM system at 2.5Gbps using multidimensional phase shift keying (PSK) codes with a single multi-port optical encoder/decoder has been demonstrated for the first time. An accurate model evaluates the power margins.

articleTitle: Fully reconfigurable compact RF photonic filters using high-Q silicon microdisk resonators
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a fully reconfigurable fourth-order SOI RF-photonic filter with a tunable bandwidth of 0.9–5 GHz, FSR > 600 GHz, out-of-band rejection > 38 dB, and compact size (0.15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) using high-Q resonator-based components.

articleTitle: Light-trails: Distributed optical grooming for emerging data-center, cloud computing, and enterprise applications
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Light-trails - generalized lightpaths - are used for provisioning emerging applications leading to the concept of spatial traffic grooming. We investigate the effects of this technology from the perspective of application support and transport.

articleTitle: Optical transmitter with 1060 nm VCSEL for low power interconnect
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An optical transmitter composed of a 90-nm CMOS driver and a high efficiency 1060 nm VCSEL is characterized. The 10 Gb Ethernet eye mask specification is met with a +33% margin with 1.7 mW/Gbps power consumption.

articleTitle: Monolithic gridless 1 × 2 wavelength-selective switch in silicon
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a monolithic 1 × 2 wavelength-selective switch in silicon nitride and silicon waveguides. The size is only 5.5 mm × 3.0 mm, and the switching is gridless with 32 pixels on a pitch of 100 GHz.

articleTitle: Dynamic model of spectral hole burning for EDFAs with 980-nm-pumping
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Spectral hole burning (SHB) in the gain spectrum of EDFAs influences the dynamic response of EDFAs and their electronic control. A 3-level-model incorporating SHB has been derived and numerically investigated. Conclusions for EDFA-control are drawn.

articleTitle: Real-time Gigabit Ethernet bidirectional transmission over a single SI-POF up to 75 meters
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper we demonstrate 1Gb/s bidirectional transmission over a single SI-POF, over the record distance of 75m. We successfully tested our system running real time Gigabit Ethernet traffic generated by a router tester.

articleTitle: Comcast optical network: A truly converged infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Comcast Corporation is one of the nation's leading providers of cable, entertainment and communication products and services, with over 23 million video customers, 17 million high-speed Internet customers and 8.5 million Comcast Digital Voice customers in 39 states plus District of Columbia. Comcast network is MEF certified and it offers business services & Cell Backhaul services over the same IP/Optical network that offers Residential triple play services. Comcast is principally involved in the development, management and operation of cable networks and in the delivery of programming content.

PACS Terms: 060.1810 Buffers, couplers, routers, switches and multiplexers

articleTitle: Distribution optical sensor system on the 610-m Guangzhou New TV Tower
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An FBG sensing network consisting of over 200 sensors are installed on the Guangzhou New TV Tower for long-term monitoring of strain, temperature and inclination to provide a mean for structural health monitoring of super-tall structures.

articleTitle: Long-haul atmospheric laser communication systems
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical communications provides an attractive means of achieving wideband data transfer over long distances. We review perceived challenges and enabling technology developments that promise to facilitate a new era of free-space laser communications.

articleTitle: Ultra high capacity transmission for optical transport network
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A collection of slides from the author's conference presentation is given. The following topics are discussed: high-capacity terrestrial system; channel rate; ultra high capacity transmission; optical transport network; pulse density modulation; PDM NGI CO-OFDM-QPSK format; and PDM higher-order QAM format.

articleTitle: Dynamic λ-OFDMA with selective multicast overlaid
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a dynamic λ-OFDMA with selective DPSK overlaid, and multicast control is realized through an alternative LO. The 10-Gb/s P2P signal, 2.5-Gb/s overlaid and 1.25-Gb/s upstream signal are transmitted 25km fiber successfully.

articleTitle: Robust design of all-optical PSK regenerator based on phase sensitive amplification
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: More compact, stable, and efficient configuration of a recently-developed regenerator is presented. The regenerator is assessed at data rates up to 56 Gbit/s using white phase noise for the first time.

articleTitle: 4×40 Gb/s all-optical wavelength conversion using SOAs and integrated arrays of ring resonators and DIs
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present 4×40Gb/s all-optical wavelength conversion employing SOAs fiber-interconnected with integrated arrays of tunable Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>-SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> micro-ring resonators and delay interferometers. We demonstrate chirp filtering and polarity inversion on-chip.

articleTitle: Demonstration of converged bidirectional OFDM-m-QAM RoF and WDM-OFDM-PON access networks
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel lightwave centralized hybrid bidirectional WDM-OFDM-PON and OFDM-m-QAM RoF network. The 11.29-Gb/s OFDM-16QAM wired DL, 5.65-Gb/s OFDM-QPSK wired UL and WiMAX downstream/upstream are successfully transmitted over 25-km SSMF.

articleTitle: φ25 mm coin-sized polarization-maintaining highly nonlinear fiber module with practical polarization crosstalk
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Down-sized polarization-maintaining highly nonlinear fiber with 100 m length is packaged into a φ25×5mm module with -22 dB of polarization crosstalk for the first time. FWM wavelength conversion bandwidth of the module is confirmed to be 52 nm.

articleTitle: A 10 Gb/s passive-components-based WDM-TDM reconfigurable optical access network architecture
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a cost-effective, reconfigurable optical access network by employing passive components in the remote node and dual conventional optical transceivers in ONUs. The architecture is demonstrated with bidirectional transmission at 10 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Layered decoding of nonbinary LDPC codes suitable for high-speed optical communications
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose using layered update rule in decoding nonbinary LDPC codes. Only 10-15 iterations suffice for good performance. Also, for the same BER performance, it increases throughput by twofold compared to conventional flooding update rule.

articleTitle: All-fiber autocorrelator based on parametric amplification
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the feasibility of an all-fiber optical autocorrelator based on parametric amplification. Our preliminary results indicate that it is possible to measure pulse widths below 100ps.

articleTitle: Enabling energy efficient exascale computing applications with optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The past few years has seen a sea change in computer architecture that will impact every facet of our society as every electronic device from cell phone to supercomputer will need to confront parallelism of unprecedented scale. Enabling future advances in sustained computational performance will require fundamental advances in computer architecture and programming models that are nothing short of reinventing computing. Photonic interconnect technologies will play an essential role to enable future progress in exascale computing.

articleTitle: High-sensitivity broadband micro-Michelson-interferometer based on an end-sphered hollow-core fiber
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a high-sensitivity broadband micro-Michelson fiber interferometer using a singlemode fiber end-spliced with a short (43.9µm) hollow-core end-collapsed lensed fiber. The extinction ratio can be above 25 dB over the 1250–1650 nm wavelength range.

articleTitle: Frame-level OEO-regenerating GPON reach extender
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a frame-level OEO-regeneration technique for GPON reach extension which overcomes the limitations of bit-level OEO-regeneration with respect to upstream efficiency and transparency.

articleTitle: Cost-effective and power-efficient extended-reach WDM/TDM PON systems
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a remote channel combine/split module for extended-reach WDM/TDM PON systems to significantly reduce initial investment with saving up to 60% and achieve good power efficiency when fully loaded with saving up to 35%.

articleTitle: Flexible and compact hierarchical optical cross-connect node with waveband add/drop restriction
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A flexible and compact hierarchical optical cross-connect (HOXC) node that considers a practical waveband add/drop restriction is proposed. We introduce a prototype HOXC system and verify its technical feasibility and transmission characteristics.

articleTitle: 25GHz hybrid silicon Mach-Zehnder modulator using high-speed push-pull slotline design
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a hybrid silicon Mach-Zehnder modulator having a voltage-length product of 2.4 V-mm and chirp parameter of -0.75. This modulator also has a modulation bandwidth of 25 GHz.

articleTitle: On an ONU for full-duplex 10.5 Gbps/λ with shared delay interferometer for format conversion and chirp filtering
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Chirped IRZ downstream is used together with a delay interferometer and a RSOA at a low complexity ONU for full-duplex 10.5Gbps transmission on a single wavelength, supported by modulation format conversion and optical offset filtering.

articleTitle: Optical dynamic random access memory (ODRAM)
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An n-bit all-optical dynamic random access memory for write, read and refresh operation in optical computing applications is investigated. The 1-bit memory element obtained by a SOA-based variable optical buffer is verified and characterized.

articleTitle: Enhancing virtual infrastructure to survive facility node failures
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose l-redundant and K-redundant schemes for the design and mapping of survivable virtual infrastructure to recover from facility node failures while minimizing network costs. The efficiency of our solutions is compared using simulation.

articleTitle: Virtualizing ADRENALINE testbed for deploying dynamic GMPLS-controlled WSON as a service
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present and evaluate the network virtualization architecture of the ADRENALINE testbed, based on virtualizing the GMPLS control plane to deploy multiple virtual networks with full control of the internal routing policies or addressing schemes.

articleTitle: Energy-efficiency of drop-and-continue traffic grooming
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper evaluates the energy-saving achievable by performing traffic grooming in WDM networks with drop-and-continue node architecture. Different grooming strategies are compared in terms of network performance and energy usage.

articleTitle: Novel dispersion controlling technique using doped ring structures within photonic crystal fibers
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We proposed the novel photonic crystal fiber structure which uses high/low doping material around each cladding holes. Through the numerical analysis, we confirmed that this fiber structure will introduce an alternative approach to control the dispersion.

articleTitle: Transmitter pre-distortion for simultaneous improvements in bit-rate, sensitivity, jitter, and power efficiency in 20 Gb/s CMOS-driven VCSEL links
publicationTitle: 2011 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exposition and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
